briefings.title: QIA, Apollo & Goldman CEOs on Global Capital
briefings.tldr: Global capital allocators emphasize that deploying capital successfully requires looking past daily noise to focus on 5-to-20-year trends, navigating an unprecedented technology supercycle, and managing structural shifts across energy, infrastructure, and geopolitical fragmentation.

briefings.title: Meta's Dina Powell McCormick: The Case for Data Centers, Backlash, AI Job Boom & Meta’s Future
briefings.tldr: Meta President and Vice Chairwoman Dina Powell McCormick joined the All-In Podcast to discuss Meta's massive data center investments, community economic impacts, the America’s Workforce Academy, the recent bipartisan teen safety settlement, and Meta's AI hardware and open-source strategy.

briefings.title: The AI Productivity Boom with David Solomon
briefings.channel: The Economic Club of New York
briefings.tldr: While AI will cause near-term job dislocation and require significant labor upskilling, it is poised to unleash a generational productivity and economic growth boom supported by massive capital market liquidity, even as businesses face rising cyber risks and macroeconomic pressures.

briefings.title: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon on Running a Bank in the Age of AI | Odd Lots
briefings.tldr: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon argues that while AI will dramatically boost productivity and reshape job structures, fears of a white-collar "job apocalypse" are overblown because emotional intelligence, trust, and human relationships remain irreplaceable business drivers.

briefings.title: 🎙️ Inside the Next Financial Crisis with Lloyd Blankfein #podcast #theforum
briefings.channel: The Economic Club of New York

people.name: Lloyd Blankfein
people.role: Former Chairman and CEO, Goldman Sachs

briefings.tldr: Lloyd Blankfein warns that a 15-year absence of a major financial reckoning has allowed overvalued, mismarked private assets to accumulate like "dry tinder" awaiting a spark.

briefings.title: Goldman Sachs Chairman on AI and the Future of Finance | The a16z Show
briefings.tldr: True risk management is rooted in contingency planning rather than prediction, requiring leaders to distinguish between being "wrong" and being "reckless" while maintaining a long-term "partnership" culture that prioritizes the institution over the individual.

briefings.title: Global Markets, World Uncertainties and the $2 Trillion Fund | Jens Stoltenberg & David Solomon
briefings.tldr: While geopolitical instability in the Middle East and structural stagnation in Europe present significant short-term risks, long-term economic optimism remains high due to the transformative productivity potential of AI and the continued compounding power of global equity markets.

briefings.title: Fmr Goldman Sachs CEO: What Surviving The 2008 Financial Crisis Taught Me — Lloyd Blankfein
briefings.tldr: Lloyd Blankfein’s career journey from Brooklyn public housing to the helm of Goldman Sachs underscores that elite leadership requires "streetwise" authenticity, the ability to pivot into "risk management mode" during uncertainty, and a commitment to radical transparency with stakeholders during existential crises.

briefings.title: Lloyd Blankfein on Private Equity, Trump, and Next Global Reckoning

people.name: Lloyd Blankfein
people.role: Former Chairman and CEO, Goldman Sachs

briefings.tldr: Lloyd Blankfein warns that while the banking system is more resilient today than in 2008, the accumulation of illiquid private credit and un-sold private equity inventory constitutes "kindling" for a future market reckoning triggered by an unpredictable spark.

briefings.title: Strikes in Iran and Lloyd Blankfein Looks Back 3/2/26
briefings.tldr: Following the death of Ayatollah Khamenei, the U.S. and Israel have entered a "new and uncertain phase" of conflict in Iran, triggering a de facto closure of the Strait of Hormuz and marking the onset of the world’s first AI-driven hot war.

briefings.title: Former Goldman Sachs CEO Talks AI, Private Credit and Politics
briefings.tldr: Former Goldman Sachs CEO Lloyd Blankfein warns that the financial markets are in the late stages of a cycle characterized by a dangerous lack of discipline in opaque assets like private credit.

briefings.title: Ben Horowitz & David Solomon on Why Scale Is The Only Thing That Matters
briefings.tldr: The current macro environment offers a "sweet spot" for financial assets, driven by significant stimulus and a capital investment super cycle that's poised to drive strong M&A and IPO activity.
